title: Portable council definition
description: The reusable half of a council: who is on it, what each seat is responsible for, how a round is run, and which sources ground each member. This is the ONLY record that may be exported or imported. It deliberately has no place to put a question, a transcript, an outcome, a chat id, or a note id, so a definition cannot carry one project's session into another.

members.description: Member identity, independent of any council seat. The same member record can be seated differently in different councils.

seats.description: A seat binds one member to one responsibility in THIS council. Identity and responsibility are separate so that neither is renamed by editing the other.

sources.description: The source inventory. Present in an export as an inventory even when the user chose not to embed the material, so a missing reference is visible at import rather than silently unsupported.

Member.description: A participant identity. member_revision advances when scope, limitations, or grounding change; a contribution records the revision it was produced from so an old answer is never re-attributed to a newer member. A functional advisor and a source-grounded simulant are the same record with different obligations: only a simulant interprets a named author, so only a simulant may carry 'represents', and it must carry grounding, a narrow scope and its known gaps. The invariants hold that line; the schema cannot.

represents.description: For a simulant, the real author or perspective being interpreted. The simulant and that person remain distinct identities; this field never asserts the person participated. A member of any other kind must leave it out.

scope.description: What this member is qualified to speak to, stated narrowly.

limitations.description: What the grounding does NOT establish. Rendered next to the member, not buried.

grounding.description: The source revisions this member was grounded on. Changing grounding is an explicit act: it selects new source_revision values and advances member_revision.

model_hint.description: Optional preferred host model id. Advisory: the host's enabled-model selection wins, and an unavailable hint is reported, never silently substituted.

role.description: Exactly one seat is the chair. The chair synthesises; advisors contribute.

relevance_tags.description: Used to pick a relevant subset for a bounded round. Selection is proposed, then shown; it is never silently narrowed.

Source.description: A captured grounding source. A source_revision pins one capture of the material: changing the content is a NEW revision, never an edit of an old one, so a past contribution can still be inspected against what it actually read.

locator.description: Where the material came from, as the user gave it: a note title, a path, a URL, or 'pasted excerpt'.

content_hash.description: Hash of the material this revision captured. It lives on the source and not only inside the payload, so an inventory entry whose content was not shared still says exactly which bytes it stood for: an import can report the drift, and material supplied later is accepted only when it hashes to this.

anchors.description: Named spans inside the captured payload that a citation may point at. An anchor with no payload present is an inventory entry: citations against it resolve to 'material not available'.

quote.description: The excerpt as captured, so a citation reads correctly even when the payload was not embedded. Capped at the same inline ceiling as any other free text: v0.1 moves whole snapshots across the host's 64 KiB IPC hop, so no single field may fill it.

DeliberationRules.description: How one consultation runs, and what it is allowed to spend. v0.1 is one bounded independent round followed by chair synthesis; the fields exist so a preset can tune it, not so the engine can grow modes implicitly. Every limit lives here rather than as a constant in the engine, so what a council may cost is inspectable in the record and travels with an exported definition.

max_concurrent_members.description: How many member calls may be in flight at once. It bounds what a round costs at any instant; max_members_per_round bounds what it costs in total.

max_prompt_bytes.description: Ceiling on the bytes of one assembled call. Council bounds what it SENDS, in bytes, because that is the quantity it can count exactly; grounding and prior contributions are dropped from the tail with a visible marker until the call fits. What a model produces is bounded by per_member_timeout_seconds and run_budget_seconds instead.

run_budget_seconds.description: Wall-clock ceiling for a whole run, chair synthesis included. A run that reaches it stops with the contributions it has and is reported partial, rather than running on unattended.

max_rounds_per_session.description: How many runs one session may hold. Nothing in the engine starts a run, so this is the ceiling on what a caller can ask of one session — the reason a client loop cannot turn one question into unbounded spend.

independent_initial_round.description: Initial member calls see the same context snapshot and their own grounding, never one another's answers. v0.1 does not offer the alternative.

preserve_disagreement.description: When true the chair must report substantive disagreement rather than resolving it into a single voice.
